data.name: Chinmayei
data.gender_notes: Chinmayei is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Chinmayei is derived from the Sanskrit words 'chinmaya' which means 'consciousness of the Absolute' and 'ei' meaning 'she'. This name symbolizes the deep spiritual understanding and connection to the divine. Chinmayei is a name for a girl who is wise, compassionate and has a strong spiritual foundation. The name Chinmayei carries the meaning “Consciousness of the Absolute” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Chinmayei usually hope their child will grow to embody consciousness of the absolute and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Chinmayei belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Consciousness of the Absolute.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Chinmayei total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.spiritual_significance: In Hindu philosophy, the pursuit of consciousness of the Absolute (Chinmaya) is considered one of the main goals of life. historical_references.reference: Chinmayi is a popular name in South India and is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Chinmaya' which means 'pure consciousness'. The name is believed to have originated during the Alwar period (9th to 12th century AD) when the Alvars, the medieval Tamil Bhakti poet-saints, composed hymns in praise of Lord Vishnu. Chinmayi is considered to be an embodiment of the goddess Aandal, one of the consorts of Lord Vishnu, in these hymns.
historical_references.context: Medieval Tamil Bhakti poetry, embodiment of goddess Aandal

historical_references.reference: Another reference to the name Chinmayi comes from the 13th century AD Hindu epic 'Mahabharata' in which there is a mention of a character named Chinmayi, the daughter of the sage Vyasa. She is an incarnation of the goddess Saraswati and is known for her deep knowledge and wisdom. The name Chinmayi signifies 'pure knowledge' or 'pure understanding' in this context.
historical_references.context: Hindu epic 'Mahabharata', incarnation of goddess Saraswati
